title: The Elder Brain's Domain
subtitle: The Mind That Dreams of Devouring the World

setting.name: The Illithid Enclave of Ch'chitl
setting.description: The mind flayer colony of Ch'chitl occupies an immense vertical cavern — a shaft so deep that its bottom has never been mapped. The colony is built into the shaft walls: platforms of pale, brain-shaped architecture connected by levitating platforms and psychic lifts, all pulsing with the sickly violet glow of concentrated psionic energy. At the shaft's center, suspended by a web of psychic force, floats the elder brain's pool — a massive stone basin filled with cerebrospinal fluid in which dwells the colony's collective intelligence. The colony is home to approximately 40 mind flayers, dozens of intellect devourers, and hundreds of thralls (enslaved humanoids whose minds have been wiped and replaced with psychic programming).
setting.atmosphere: Oppressive, alien, and deeply wrong. The psychic pressure in Ch'chitl is constant — a low hum of alien thought that presses against the edges of consciousness, probing for weakness. The architecture is organic and unsettling, all curves and folds that resemble brain tissue more than stone. The mind flayers move silently, their tentacle-faces expressionless, communicating in psychic whispers that non-illithids perceive as headache-inducing static. Everything here is designed to serve the elder brain — every structure, every creature, every thought.

keyLocations.name: The Approach Tunnels
keyLocations.description: The tunnels leading to Ch'chitl have been smoothed by centuries of mind flayer passage, their walls bearing territorial markers in Qualith — the illithid tactile language. Intellect devourers patrol the perimeter, hiding in the bodies of thralls that appear to be lost travelers or Underdark wanderers. The psychic pressure increases with every step closer to the colony.
features: Smoothed walls bearing Qualith territorial markers and warnings
Increasing psychic pressure (DC 12 Wisdom save every hour or gain 1 level of exhaustion from psychic strain, reduced to DC 10 with the psychic disruptor fragment)
Thrall patrols — humanoids whose minds have been replaced with mind flayer programming, appearing normal until combat
A deep gnome resistance outpost hidden in a side tunnel, operated by survivors from Blingdenstone
encounters: 2 intellect devourers hiding in the bodies of 'lost travelers' who approach the party seeking help
A thrall patrol of 4 mind-wiped humanoids who attack on psychic command if the party is detected
The deep gnome resistance — svirfneblin guerrillas who have been fighting the mind flayers and can provide intelligence
secrets: The deep gnome resistance has found a way to temporarily block the elder brain's psychic detection using a mineral called psionically resonant quartz — they can provide the party with enough to shield themselves for approximately 4 hours inside the colony

The approach tunnels are monitored by the elder brain through a network of psychic sensor nodes embedded in the walls — small, brain-like growths that can be identified (DC 16 Perception) and destroyed

keyLocations.name: The Colony Perimeter — Upper Platforms
keyLocations.description: The outermost ring of the colony, where the thrall barracks, food processing chambers (where humanoid brains are prepared for consumption), and the breeding pools for intellect devourers are located. This is the most lightly defended area of the colony but also the most disturbing.
features: Thrall barracks — rows of cots where mind-wiped humanoids sleep in eerie silence between tasks
Processing chambers — rooms where captured humanoids are restrained and their brains extracted (deeply disturbing to witness)
Intellect devourer breeding pools — shallow basins of cerebrospinal fluid where new intellect devourers gestate
Levitating platforms that connect the upper tier to the middle and lower tiers (activated by psychic command, but can be tricked with DC 15 Arcana)
encounters: 1 mind flayer with 4 thralls, processing a new batch of captives
A group of captives not yet processed — potential rescues who provide intelligence about the colony layout
secrets: The intellect devourer breeding pools are vulnerable — destroying them (they have AC 5, 20 HP each, vulnerable to psychic damage) would prevent the colony from replacing its losses
Among the captives is a drow spy sent by Ilvara to negotiate with the mind flayers — she carries proof of the elder brain's plans for the surface world

keyLocations.name: The Inner Sanctum — Mind Flayer Quarter
keyLocations.description: The middle tier of the colony where the mind flayers live, work, and scheme. Elegant chambers carved in the organic, brain-like architecture house individual illithids and their experiments. A central meeting chamber serves as the colony's agora, where mind flayers gather to share thoughts and receive directives from the elder brain. The psychic pressure here is intense.
features: Individual mind flayer chambers, each reflecting its occupant's particular obsession (one studies portal magic, another breeds improved intellect devourers, a third catalogs stolen memories)
The Agora — a circular chamber where the elder brain's psychic voice is clearest, used for colony-wide communication
A research laboratory where the drow biological weapons research is being studied and improved
The Arcanist's Chamber — home to a mind flayer arcanist (a rare illithid spellcaster) who guards the path to the elder brain
encounters: 2-3 mind flayers at any given time in the Agora
1 mind flayer arcanist (CR 8) guarding the descent to the elder brain's pool
Thrall servants throughout, who will alert mind flayers if they detect intruders
secrets: The mind flayer arcanist is secretly dissatisfied with the elder brain's plans — it has developed individual ambitions, which is heresy in illithid society. It might be turned into a reluctant ally if approached correctly

The research lab contains the fruits of the drow-illithid collaboration: a prototype psychic amplification device that could extend the elder brain's influence to the surface world. Destroying it is a secondary objective

keyLocations.name: The Elder Brain's Pool
keyLocations.description: The deepest point of the colony and the center of the mind flayers' world. A massive stone basin, fifty feet across, filled with glowing cerebrospinal fluid in which floats the elder brain — a brain the size of a wagon, trailing nerve-like tendrils that connect to every part of the colony through psychic channels. The pool is suspended in the center of the vertical shaft by arches of psychically reinforced stone, with a narrow bridge providing the only physical access. The elder brain's psychic presence here is overwhelming — standing near the pool is like standing in a hurricane of alien thought.
features: The elder brain's pool (50 ft diameter, 10 ft deep, filled with cerebrospinal fluid)
A narrow stone bridge (5 ft wide, 30 ft long) connecting the platform to the pool's edge
Psychic amplification nodes around the pool's rim — destroying them weakens the elder brain's defenses
The elder brain itself — a massive, pulsating brain with nerve-like tendrils, floating in glowing fluid
A vertical shaft above and below the pool, dropping into unfathomable darkness
encounters: The Elder Brain (CR 14) — the campaign's final boss, a terrifyingly powerful psionic entity
2 mind flayers that serve as the elder brain's personal guard
4 intellect devourers that emerge from the fluid at the elder brain's command
secrets: The elder brain's plan is to use the combined technologies stolen from the drow and aboleth to extend its psychic influence to the surface world, creating a network of thralls that would give it control over surface civilization within a generation
The elder brain is vulnerable when its psychic amplification nodes are destroyed — without them, its psychic range contracts to the immediate area and its legendary resistances are reduced

If the psychic disruptor fragment from scenario 3 is activated near the pool, it disrupts the elder brain's control over the colony, causing temporary chaos as mind flayers lose their telepathic coordination

synopsis: The campaign reaches its climax as the party enters the mind flayer colony of Ch'chitl to confront the elder brain — the vast psychic intelligence that has been pulling strings throughout the Underdark. With intelligence gathered from all previous scenarios, allies gained along the way, and the psychic disruptor fragment from the aboleth's temple, the party must infiltrate the colony, navigate its nightmare architecture, and reach the elder brain's pool for a final confrontation. The elder brain's plan to extend its psychic influence to the surface world must be stopped, or the entire world — not just the Underdark — will fall under its control.
hook: All roads lead here. The drow weapons program, the aboleth's alliance, the psychic whispers that have haunted the party since the Fungal Caverns — they all originate from the elder brain of Ch'chitl. The deep gnome resistance provides the final pieces of intelligence: the colony's layout, the elder brain's vulnerabilities, and a narrow window of opportunity when the colony's defenses will be at their weakest — during the elder brain's periodic communion, when it draws all its psychic power inward. The party must strike now, or the elder brain will complete its surface-world infiltration network and become unstoppable.

acts.title: Act 1: Into the Hive
acts.description: The party approaches the mind flayer colony, meets the deep gnome resistance, and infiltrates the outer perimeter. They encounter the horrors of the colony's operations and must deal with intellect devourers, thralls, and the ever-present psychic pressure.
objectives: Make contact with the deep gnome resistance
Rescue captives and/or destroy the intellect devourer breeding pools

scenes.name: The Last Free Minds
scenes.description: The party reaches the deep gnome resistance outpost in the tunnels near Ch'chitl and receives final intelligence and equipment for the assault on the colony.
scenes.readAloud: "The tunnel narrows and the psychic pressure that has been building for hours becomes a physical sensation — a throb behind your eyes, a buzz in your teeth. Then a small figure appears from a hidden crevice in the wall, no taller than a child but with the eyes of a veteran soldier. The svirfneblin holds up a hand — wait. She examines each of you with a practiced gaze, then nods. 'You are still yourselves,' she says. 'That is good. Many who come this close to the hive are not.' She leads you through a concealed passage to a small cavern where a dozen more deep gnomes wait — thin, hard-eyed, and armed. Maps cover the walls, drawn in mineral pigments on stone. At the center, a rough table holds chunks of a crystalline mineral that thrums with a faint, soothing vibration — a counterpoint to the oppressive psychic hum. 'Resonant quartz,' the svirfneblin leader says. 'It blocks the brain's eyes. You will have four hours once you activate it. After that...' She draws a finger across her throat."

skillChecks.success: The deep gnome resistance fighters are exhausted and desperate but dedicated. They have been fighting the mind flayers for years, losing people regularly. This mission is their best chance — and likely their last, if it fails.
skillChecks.failure: The deep gnomes seem competent and professional, but the depth of their commitment and sacrifice is not immediately apparent.

skillChecks.success: You understand the resonant quartz mechanism — it creates a psychic 'dead zone' around the bearer, preventing the elder brain from detecting thoughts within its radius. The four-hour limitation is because the quartz absorbs psychic energy and eventually overloads, shattering.
skillChecks.failure: The quartz clearly has psychic properties but the specifics of how it works are unclear.

skillChecks.success: You recall lore about elder brains — they are the culmination of a mind flayer colony, containing the accumulated knowledge and personalities of every mind flayer that has died in the colony's history. Destroying one is a devastating blow to the illithid race but will not eliminate the colony entirely — the surviving mind flayers will flee to join other colonies.
skillChecks.failure: Elder brains are powerful psionic entities, but the specifics of their nature and vulnerabilities are unclear.

scenes.roleplayNotes: The deep gnome resistance provides the final exposition and equipment the party needs. Play them as battle-hardened guerrilla fighters who have seen terrible things — they have lost friends to ceremorphosis (the process of a mind flayer tadpole consuming a humanoid brain and transforming the body), rescued survivors from the processing chambers, and lived under the constant threat of detection. Their leader, Senni Gemcutter, is calm, precise, and utterly committed. This scene should feel like the briefing before a special operations mission — detailed, methodical, and tinged with the awareness that not everyone may come back.
loot: Resonant quartz shards (enough for 4 hours of psychic shielding for the entire party)
Deep gnome intelligence packet: detailed map of the colony, guard rotation schedules, location of the elder brain's pool
2 potions of greater healing from the resistance's medical supplies
4 vials of mind blank oil (uncommon consumable — when applied to the forehead, grants advantage on Intelligence and Wisdom saving throws for 1 hour)

scenes.name: The Horror Above
scenes.description: The party enters the colony's outer perimeter and witnesses the full horror of mind flayer civilization — thrall barracks, processing chambers, and intellect devourer breeding pools.
scenes.readAloud: "The colony entrance is unremarkable — a smooth archway in the tunnel wall, unmarked except for Qualith carvings that your fingers dare not touch. Beyond it, the tunnel opens into a vertical shaft so vast that your light cannot find the far wall. Platforms of pale, organic-looking stone jut from the shaft walls at staggered heights, connected by bridges that glow with faint psychic light. The architecture is wrong — all curves and folds and structures that look disturbingly like enlarged brain tissue. And on the nearest platform, you see them: rows of cots, perfectly aligned, where humanoids of every race lie in silent, motionless sleep. Dozens of them. Their eyes are open. They are not dreaming. Their minds have been emptied like vessels, waiting to be filled with psychic commands. This is what the elder brain does with its food."

skillChecks.success: The resonant quartz and careful movement keep the party undetected as they navigate the upper platforms. Thralls pass by without reacting, and the distant shapes of mind flayers on lower platforms do not look up.
skillChecks.failure: A thrall's residual instincts cause it to stare at the party for a long, terrible moment before its programming reasserts and it looks away. The near-detection costs the party their confidence — disadvantage on the next Stealth check.

skillChecks.success: You identify a way to temporarily restore awareness to a thrall — a specific combination of pressure points and adrenaline can break through the psychic programming for a few minutes, long enough to gather intelligence.
skillChecks.failure: The thralls are beyond medical help — their minds have been completely overwritten.

skillChecks.success: Among the captives in the processing queue, you find the drow spy sent by Ilvara. She carries evidence of the elder brain's surface infiltration plan — thrall agents already placed in surface cities, waiting to be activated.
skillChecks.failure: The captives are too traumatized to provide useful intelligence about the colony.

enemies: 3 thralls (use commoner stats but with mindless condition — immune to frightened, charmed)
combatEncounters.tactics: The intellect devourers are the real threat — they hide inside two of the thralls, bursting out when the party gets close. Their Devour Intellect ability (DC 12 Intelligence save or 2d10 psychic damage, incapacitated until end of next turn on failure) is devastating. The remaining thrall attacks mindlessly. The intellect devourers attempt to use Body Thief on any incapacitated character — if successful, they take control of the body and try to lead the party into a mind flayer ambush.
combatEncounters.terrain: Colony upper platform (60 ft by 40 ft). Rows of thrall cots provide half cover. The platform edge drops into the vertical shaft — a fall of hundreds of feet. Processing chamber doors are closed but not locked. The psychic ambient light provides dim illumination throughout.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This scene should be deeply disturbing. The mind flayer colony is not a dungeon full of monsters — it is a factory that processes sentient beings into resources. The thralls are the most horrifying element: people who have been stripped of everything that made them individuals and reduced to biological machines. Do not shy away from the horror, but balance it with determination — this is why the party is here. Every thrall they see is a reason to destroy the elder brain. If the party finds the drow spy, she provides crucial intelligence but is also Ilvara's agent — a complication for later.
loot: Drow spy's evidence packet: surface infiltration plans (quest item — reveals the elder brain's broader agenda)
From the processing chambers: confiscated equipment including a +1 longbow, a set of mithral chain mail, and 200 gp in mixed coins taken from captives
Intellect devourer brains (if preserved, worth 100 gp each to the right buyer for research purposes)

acts.title: Act 2: Heart of Darkness
acts.description: The party descends deeper into the colony, navigating the mind flayer quarter and confronting the mind flayer arcanist who guards the descent to the elder brain's pool. They must find a way past the colony's inner defenses.
objectives: Navigate to the middle tier of the colony
Explore the mind flayer quarter without being detected
Destroy the prototype psychic amplification device in the research lab
Confront or bypass the mind flayer arcanist
Reach the descent to the elder brain's pool

scenes.name: Among the Mind Flayers
scenes.description: The party moves through the mind flayer living quarters, witnessing illithid society and its alien operations, while searching for the research laboratory and the way down to the elder brain.
scenes.readAloud: "The levitating platform descends silently, carrying you deeper into the colony's shaft. The architecture here is more refined — smooth curves of pale stone that pulse with inner light, chambers sealed by membranes of psychic energy rather than doors, and corridors wide enough for the mind flayers to glide through in their long, dark robes. You see one — the first mind flayer you have encountered up close. It stands seven feet tall, its body emaciated beneath flowing robes, its head a bulbous mass from which four long tentacles hang like a grotesque beard. Its white, pupilless eyes sweep the corridor without seeing you — the resonant quartz holds — and it passes by in a whisper of psychic static that makes your skull ache. The corridor ahead branches: one path leads to a chamber thrumming with contained energy — the research lab. The other descends further, toward a psychic pressure so intense it makes your vision blur. The elder brain. It is close."

skillChecks.success: You navigate the mind flayer quarter without alerting any illithids. The resonant quartz blocks psychic detection, and your physical stealth prevents visual detection.
skillChecks.failure: A mind flayer pauses near the party, its tentacles writhing as if sensing something it cannot quite identify. It does not raise the alarm but begins sweeping the area with enhanced psychic detection — the party must move quickly or be found.

skillChecks.success: You identify the research laboratory's prototype psychic amplifier and understand how to destroy it safely. A controlled overload will destroy the device without alerting the elder brain immediately.
skillChecks.failure: The device is clearly dangerous but you are not sure how to destroy it without causing a catastrophic psychic explosion that would alert the entire colony.

skillChecks.success: If the party encounters the mind flayer arcanist, you appeal to its secret individual ambitions. It will not betray the colony openly but will 'conveniently' be elsewhere when the party passes, allowing access to the descent.
skillChecks.failure: The mind flayer arcanist is loyal to its nature and attacks immediately.

enemies: 1 mind flayer arcanist (CR 8, use mind flayer stats but add 3rd-level spellcasting: counterspell, fireball, shield, and 4th-level: dimension door, Evard's black tentacles)
combatEncounters.tactics: The arcanist uses dimension door to maintain distance, casting Evard's black tentacles to restrain the party while using Mind Blast (DC 15 Intelligence save, 4d8+4 psychic damage, stunned on fail). It uses shield and counterspell defensively. If reduced below half HP, it attempts to flee using dimension door to alert the elder brain. Preventing its escape is critical to maintaining surprise.
combatEncounters.terrain: Circular chamber (30 ft diameter) with a central pillar of psychic crystal. The pillar provides total cover from one direction. Psychic membranes seal the exits — they can be passed through but slow movement (5 ft of movement to pass through). The descent to the elder brain's pool is through a shaft in the chamber floor.

scenes.roleplayNotes: The mind flayer quarter should feel like being behind enemy lines in the most alien possible environment. Everything is wrong — the architecture, the sounds, the smell, the constant psychic pressure. The mind flayers themselves should be played as terrifyingly intelligent and utterly inhuman — they do not hate the party, they simply view them as food or tools. The arcanist is the most complex mind flayer NPC: it has developed individual ambitions, which is heresy in illithid society. If the party can appeal to its ambition rather than its loyalty, they can bypass the hardest fight before the final boss.
loot: Prototype psychic amplifier components (if destroyed carefully — worth 500 gp to arcane researchers, or can be repurposed as a one-time psychic bomb: 30-ft radius, DC 15 Intelligence save, 8d6 psychic damage)
Mind flayer arcanist's spellbook (if defeated — contains alien versions of standard spells, worth 200 gp to a wizard or can be studied to learn counterspell and dimension door)

A tentacle rod (rare, requires attunement — 3 charges, each charge allows a tentacle attack: +9 to hit, reach 15 ft, 1d6 psychic damage and DC 13 Constitution save or poisoned for 1 minute; regains 1d3 charges at dawn)

scenes.name: The Descent
scenes.description: The party descends the shaft to the elder brain's pool, the psychic pressure building to nearly unbearable levels. This is the point of no return.
scenes.readAloud: "The shaft descends vertically, and you climb down using handholds carved into the smooth stone. With each foot of descent, the psychic pressure intensifies. The resonant quartz in your pockets vibrates harder, growing warm. A voice enters your mind — not words but pure will, vast and cold and utterly certain of its own supremacy. The elder brain knows something is wrong. It cannot see you through the quartz, but it feels your absence — a void in its omniscience, moving closer. It is curious. It is amused. And beneath the amusement, for the first time, you sense something else: it is calculating the threat you represent. Below, the shaft opens into a chamber of impossible scale. At its center, suspended by arches of stone and psychic force, floats a pool of glowing fluid. And in the pool, something vast and terrible waits. Your resonant quartz begins to crack."

skillChecks.success: You withstand the elder brain's psychic pressure without faltering, maintaining your focus and determination as you descend to the final confrontation.
skillChecks.failure: The psychic pressure staggers you. You gain one level of exhaustion from the psychic strain and have disadvantage on the first saving throw against the elder brain's abilities.

skillChecks.success: You descend the shaft quickly and safely, reaching the elder brain's chamber with the resonant quartz still functional.
skillChecks.failure: You slip on the smooth stone and catch yourself, but the jarring impact cracks your resonant quartz. You lose psychic shielding 1 round earlier than expected.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is the atmospheric bridge to the final confrontation. Make it feel like a descent into the heart of something vast and alien. The elder brain's psychic voice should be unlike anything the party has encountered — not words, not images, but pure intent and will. It is not angry. It is not afraid. It is assessing the threat with the cold precision of an intelligence that has consumed thousands of minds over centuries. The cracking of the resonant quartz adds a ticking clock — the party's psychic shielding is failing, and time is running out.

acts.title: Act 3: The Battle of Minds
acts.description: The campaign's climactic confrontation with the elder brain. The party must defeat or destroy the elder brain in its pool, using everything they have gathered throughout the campaign — the psychic disruptor, allies' blessings, intelligence about vulnerabilities, and their own courage.
objectives: Confront the elder brain in its pool
Destroy the psychic amplification nodes around the pool to weaken its defenses
Activate the psychic disruptor fragment (if available) to disrupt the colony
Defeat the elder brain before reinforcements overwhelm the party

scenes.name: The Mind That Dreams
scenes.description: The final battle. The party faces the elder brain and its guards in the pool chamber, fighting against overwhelming psychic power while the resonant quartz fails and the colony begins to respond to the threat.
scenes.readAloud: "The chamber opens before you like the inside of a skull. The walls curve inward, smooth and organic, pulsing with veins of psychic light that converge on the pool at the center. And there it floats — the elder brain. It is enormous, larger than any creature you have fought — a brain the size of a cart, its surface covered in folds and convolutions that glow with inner light, trailing nerve-like tendrils that extend into the pool's fluid and into the walls themselves, connecting to the entire colony. Two mind flayers stand at the pool's edge, their tentacles writhing, their white eyes fixed on you. And from the pool, smaller shapes surface — brain-like creatures with bestial legs that scramble onto the stone platform and turn toward you with predatory intent. Intellect devourers. The elder brain turns its attention to you fully, and the weight of it is staggering. The resonant quartz in your hands cracks, then shatters, and for the first time, you hear its voice clearly — a voice that has consumed a thousand lifetimes of memory and found them all... insufficient. 'I have dreamed of worlds,' it says, 'and in my dreams, they kneel. You are the last inconvenience before my dream becomes reality. How... tedious.'"

skillChecks.success: You identify the 6 psychic amplification nodes around the pool's rim. Each node has AC 13 and 15 HP. For each node destroyed, the elder brain's psychic abilities are weakened: -1 to its spell save DC, -1 to its psychic attack bonus, and one of its legendary resistances is removed (at 3 nodes destroyed).
skillChecks.failure: The nodes are visible but their function is unclear. You must discover their purpose through trial and error.

skillChecks.success: You withstand the psychic backlash as the resonant quartz shatters, maintaining your composure and readiness for battle.
skillChecks.failure: The quartz shattering sends a spike of psychic pain through you. You are stunned until the end of your next turn.

enemies: 1 Elder Brain (CR 14, see below for modifications)
combatEncounters.tactics: The elder brain fights from its pool, using Psychic Link (DC 18 Intelligence save, range 120 ft — on failure, the elder brain controls the target's actions on the elder brain's next turn), Tentacle attacks (reach 30 ft from pool edge, +9 to hit, 3d8+4 psychic damage), and Mind Blast (60-ft cone from pool, DC 18 Intelligence save, 5d10+5 psychic damage, stunned on failure). It has 3 legendary actions per round and 3 legendary resistances. Legendary Actions: Tentacle Attack (1 action), Break Concentration (2 actions — targets one concentrating creature, DC 16 Con save), Psychic Pulse (3 actions — all creatures within 60 ft make DC 16 Wis save or take 2d10 psychic damage). The mind flayers engage in melee with their own Mind Blast and Extract Brain abilities. The intellect devourers target stunned or incapacitated characters with Body Thief. Reinforcements: If combat lasts more than 8 rounds, 2 additional mind flayers arrive from the shaft above. If the psychic disruptor fragment is activated, the elder brain loses 1 legendary resistance and all intellect devourers are stunned for 2 rounds. If 3+ amplification nodes are destroyed, the elder brain's save DCs are reduced by 2 and it loses all remaining legendary resistances. When reduced to 0 HP, the elder brain lets out a psychic death scream — all creatures within 120 ft make DC 18 Wisdom save or take 4d10 psychic damage and be stunned for 1 round.
combatEncounters.terrain: Elder brain chamber (80 ft diameter circular). Central pool (50 ft diameter, 10 ft deep). Narrow stone bridge (5 ft wide, 30 ft long) from platform to pool edge. 6 psychic amplification nodes spaced around the pool's rim. The bridge provides no cover. The pool's fluid is dangerous — any non-illithid creature entering it takes 2d6 psychic damage per round. The shaft above and the darkness below provide escape routes but also entry points for reinforcements.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is it — the campaign's final battle. Make it feel epic, terrifying, and meaningful. The elder brain should be the most dangerous and intelligent opponent the party has ever faced. It adapts its tactics — if the party targets the nodes, it prioritizes defending them. If a character is stunned, it commands the intellect devourers to go for the kill. Its dialogue is constant psychic commentary: contemptuous, curious, and increasingly desperate as the fight turns against it. When it dies, the psychic scream should feel like an earthquake of the mind — every thought the elder brain ever consumed, centuries of stolen memories, erupting outward in a cascade of fragmentary images and emotions before dissolving into silence. The colony begins to collapse — not physically but psychically. Without the elder brain, the mind flayers lose their coordination and cohesion. They scatter, flee, or are consumed by panic. The party must escape before the colony implodes.
loot: Elder brain residue: crystallized psychic fluid from the pool (worth 1000 gp to arcane researchers, or can be crafted into a headband of intellect by a skilled artificer)

Elder brain's accumulated hoard (scattered on the pool floor): 800 gp in ancient coins, a ring of mind shielding (rare, requires attunement), a wand of fear (rare, requires attunement, 7 charges), a gem of seeing (rare, requires attunement)
Mind flayer equipment: 2 tentacle rods, 2 sets of mind flayer robes (AC 12, resistant to psychic damage)

scenes.name: The Long Climb Home
scenes.description: With the elder brain destroyed, the mind flayer colony descends into chaos. The party must escape the collapsing psychic infrastructure and make their way back to the surface, aided by allies they have gathered throughout the campaign.
scenes.readAloud: "The elder brain's death scream fades into silence, and for one perfect, crystalline moment, the Underdark is still. Then the colony begins to unravel. The psychic light in the walls flickers and dies. The levitating platforms shudder, some crashing into the shaft walls. Mind flayers stagger, clutching their heads, their coordination shattered — some flee into the tunnels, others simply collapse. The thralls awaken screaming as minds that were wiped clean suddenly face the void where their identities used to be. The shaft groans as the psychic infrastructure that held it together fails. 'Time to go,' someone says — it does not matter who. You run. Up through the disintegrating colony, past panicking mind flayers too confused to attack, through corridors where the walls themselves seem to be breathing their last. The deep gnome resistance is waiting at the perimeter, their faces a mix of disbelief and fierce joy. 'You did it,' Senni whispers. 'You actually did it.' The tunnels beyond the colony are clear. The psychic pressure that has haunted your every step in the Underdark is gone — truly gone — for the first time. The silence feels like freedom. And somewhere far above, the surface world waits, unaware of how close it came to dreaming a monster's dream forever."

skillChecks.success: You navigate the collapsing colony quickly, avoiding falling debris and failing platforms.
skillChecks.failure: A section of platform collapses beneath you. DC 14 Dexterity save or take 3d6 bludgeoning damage from the fall.

skillChecks.success: You lead the group through the tunnel network back toward familiar territory, retracing the path from the Darklake.
skillChecks.failure: The route is confusing in the aftermath of the colony's collapse. You lose several hours finding your way and gain 1 level of exhaustion.

skillChecks.success: You rally the freed thralls who are coherent enough to move, guiding them toward the deep gnome resistance for care and eventual return to their homes.
skillChecks.failure: The freed thralls are too traumatized to respond and must be left with the deep gnomes.

combatEncounters.tactics: This is a gauntlet encounter — desperate, disoriented enemies attacking during the escape. The mind flayer is panicked and its Mind Blast recharges on a 6 only (instead of 5-6). The intellect devourers attack the nearest creature, friend or foe. This fight should feel like an aftershock, not a major battle.
combatEncounters.terrain: Collapsing corridor (10-15 ft wide). Debris falls periodically (DC 11 Dex save each round or take 1d6 bludgeoning). The corridor leads to the colony exit and safety.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is the campaign's epilogue. The tone should shift from desperate combat to exhausted triumph. The escape is dangerous but not as threatening as what came before — the worst is over. The deep gnome resistance's reaction provides validation — they have been fighting this war for years, and the party just won it. The freed thralls are a reminder of what was at stake and what the mind flayers did to real people. End the campaign with a sense of hard-won victory and the promise of a world saved from a threat it never even knew existed. The party has gone to the deepest, darkest place in the world and brought back light.
loot: Deep gnome gratitude: a lifetime of welcome in Blingdenstone, a masterwork svirfneblin dagger (functions as a +1 dagger that glows when mind flayers are within 120 ft), 500 gp reward from the resistance's war fund
Salvaged thrall equipment: assorted weapons, armor, and personal effects (300 gp total value, or can be returned to the thralls' families)

Campaign completion reward: the knowledge that the elder brain's surface infiltration plan has been stopped, the drow-illithid alliance is shattered, and the Underdark is freer than it has been in centuries

npcsInvolved.name: Senni Gemcutter
npcsInvolved.description: The leader of the deep gnome resistance, a small but fierce svirfneblin woman with close-cropped white hair and eyes that have seen too much. She moves with the quiet efficiency of someone who has lived under constant threat of discovery for years. Every word is measured, every action deliberate.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Senni has dedicated her life to fighting the mind flayers after they destroyed her home settlement and took her brother for ceremorphosis. She leads the resistance with an iron will and a strategic mind, but she knows they cannot defeat the elder brain alone. The party is her best chance — and she will give them everything she has to ensure their success.

npcsInvolved.name: The Mind Flayer Arcanist
npcsInvolved.description: A rare mind flayer who has developed arcane spellcasting ability — a trait viewed with suspicion by the elder brain, which prefers its subjects to rely solely on psionics. Taller than most illithids, it wears robes covered in arcane symbols that seem to writhe independently of the fabric. Its four tentacles move with unusual expressiveness.
npcsInvolved.motivation: The arcanist has developed something almost unheard of in illithid society: individual ambition. It chafes under the elder brain's absolute control and has been secretly studying ways to free itself from the psychic hierarchy. It will not openly betray the colony, but if offered a credible path to independence, it might step aside at a critical moment.

npcsInvolved.name: The Elder Brain of Ch'chitl
npcsInvolved.description: A brain the size of a wagon, floating in a pool of glowing cerebrospinal fluid, trailing nerve-like tendrils that connect to every part of the colony. It contains the accumulated memories and personalities of centuries of dead mind flayers, making it one of the most intelligent and knowledgeable entities in the Underdark. Its 'voice' is not sound but pure psychic will — thoughts that arrive in your mind as absolute certainties.
npcsInvolved.motivation: The elder brain seeks to extend its psychic influence to the surface world, creating a network of thralls in surface cities that would give it de facto control over civilization within a generation. It has been patient — decades of planning, manipulating the drow and the aboleth, building its psychic amplification network. The party represents the first real threat to its plan, and it intends to consume their minds and add their knowledge to its own.

rewards.gold: 2600 gp total (elder brain hoard, salvaged equipment, deep gnome reward, misc loot)
items: Ring of Mind Shielding (rare, requires attunement)
Wand of Fear (rare, requires attunement, 7 charges)
Headband of Intellect (if crafted from elder brain residue, rare, requires attunement)
Svirfneblin Dagger (+1, glows near mind flayers)
rewards.story: The elder brain of Ch'chitl is destroyed, shattering the mind flayer colony and ending the psychic threat to the Underdark and the surface world. The drow-illithid alliance is broken. The freed thralls can eventually be returned to their homes. The deep gnome resistance has won their war. The party has traveled from the beautiful but threatened Fungal Caverns, through the cruel elegance of drow society, across the ancient waters of the Sunless Sea, and into the heart of psychic darkness itself — and emerged victorious. The Underdark will never be safe, but it is freer than it has been in centuries, and the world above will never know how close it came to enslavement.

twists: The elder brain has already placed thrall agents in surface cities — even destroying it does not immediately eliminate the threat, creating potential hooks for future adventures.
The mind flayer arcanist can be turned from an enemy into a reluctant non-combatant through appealing to its individual ambitions — a rare moment of nuance in dealing with mind flayers.
The elder brain's psychic death scream frees the thralls but also traumatizes them — some will never fully recover, creating a bittersweet victory.
The drow spy found among the captives carries proof that Ilvara was unknowingly serving the elder brain all along — if she survives, she becomes an unlikely ally against the mind flayer remnants.

The elder brain's last act is to psychically transmit its accumulated knowledge to other elder brains across the Underdark — the party's victory is total for Ch'chitl but the illithid race has not been defeated, only set back.
dmTips: The mind flayer colony should feel like the most dangerous and alien place the party has ever been. Every other scenario was preparation for this. Use the accumulated goodwill and experience from earlier scenarios — the psychic disruptor from the aboleth's temple, the intelligence from the drow outpost, the allies gained along the way — to make the party feel like their choices mattered.

The elder brain fight should be the hardest, most dynamic combat of the campaign. Use its legendary actions to maintain constant pressure, target different characters with different abilities, and adapt to the party's tactics. If the party is too strong, add reinforcements. If they are struggling, have an ally (the arcanist, Senni's guerrillas) create a distraction. The fight should feel desperate but winnable.

The psychic amplification nodes around the pool are the key to making the elder brain fight manageable. Destroying them should feel like a meaningful tactical achievement — describe the elder brain's reaction as each one is destroyed (it goes from contemptuous to concerned to desperate).

The escape from the collapsing colony should be exciting but not punishing — the party has earned their victory. Use it to tie up loose threads (freed thralls, deep gnome gratitude, mind flayer remnants fleeing) rather than to threaten a TPK.

End the campaign with weight and meaning. The party has done something extraordinary — they have saved the world from an enemy it never knew existed. Let them feel the weight of that accomplishment, even if the world above will never know what happened in the lightless depths below.
